title: *WATCH OUR NEW AIPAC DOCUMENTARY* Zeteo Pulls Back the Curtain on the Pro-Israel Lobby
author: Team Zeteo
content:
**Zeteo 's** latest investigative documentary is here! You can watch it in
full above, if you are, or become, a **[paid
subscriber.](http://zeteo.com/subscribe)**

**' Night Flower: Inside AIPAC's Fight for Influence'** examines evidence that
raises questions about whether AIPAC's relationship with the Israeli
government should require the organization to register as a foreign agent
under U.S. law.

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

Watch the groundbreaking film above, which follows the powerful and polarizing
pro-Israel lobby from its roots as a one-man advocacy operation to the present
day, where it's playing a key role in the U.S. midterm elections. It features
interviews with multiple former AIPAC officials and insiders, members of
Congress such as Reps. Thomas Massie and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, and leading
activists as it examines America's most influential pro-Israel lobbying group.

**" Always remember, a lobby is a night flower,"** former AIPAC staffer M.J.
Rosenberg recalls being told on his first day. **" It blossoms in the dark and
withers in the sun."**

AIPAC has long fought efforts to register under the Foreign Agents
Registration Act (FARA), stating that it operates as an American organization
with no direction from the Israeli government. But interviews by the **' Night
Flower' **team question that assertion by tracing evidence in cases over the
past four decades.

In a startling disclosure, a longtime AIPAC employee granted anonymity to
speak candidly about his decision to break with the group, says that AIPAC
operates as a foreign agent for Israel in spirit, if not the letter of the
law. **" There are times when it seems pretty clear that AIPAC is just doing
Israel's bidding. Without question, without comment."**

And in one revealing interview, **correspondent Dion Nissenbaum** questions
**former AIPAC employee Keith Weissman** about his role in a high-profile
espionage case and if he passed on confidential information from a Pentagon
source to Israeli officials. **" Yes, absolutely. I admit that freely,"**
Weissman says in the film. **" I did pass it on to the Embassy of Israel."**

The film, from 1st and Orchard Films, is the work of **Dion Nissenbaum,** a
two-time Pulitzer Prize finalist and the filmmaker behind **Zeteo 's** '[Who
Killed Shireen](https://zeteo.com/s/who-killed-shireen),' and **Zach
Goldbaum** , the Emmy Award-winning director behind the 2024 New York Times
Opinion film 'Meet the World's Most Honorable Bank Robbers of Lebanon.'

The film premiered last night in Chicago, with future screenings planned in
the coming weeks.

**AIPAC 's Response**

In response to the questions posed in this film, AIPAC Spokeswoman Deryn Sousa
denied any wrongdoing and said:

_" AIPAC is an American organization. Our members and board leadership are all
Americans, and our funding comes exclusively from Americans. We advocate for
the U.S.-Israel relationship because we believe it is good for America. We
make our own decisions, set our own policies, and take direction from one
place: the AIPAC Board."_

_" Suggesting that pro-Israel Americans should register with the government as
foreign agents because of their views on American foreign policy is an attack
on our most basic American freedom. We reject that premise entirely."_

AIPAC also said the confidential 1984 US trade report handed to the lobbying
group by an Israeli Embassy official was "an unsolicited document that AIPAC
returned."

The organization also disputed allegations of what was said by Howard Kohr
after the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks, saying, "Those quotations do not accurately
reflect what was said."

And on the Israeli Foreign Minister
[tweet](https://urldefense.com/v3/__https://x.com/Israel_katz/status/1792636886407676303__;!!FZnJprQ!Fwfj4blqpKUT1eqWQ9EgaWYYlmdGy80vAlYxbmvZ92O-lv0dUJo2wbndzU6fIkEUrTZ-
PMCXyaw2qRJrMuxl7ZA$) describing a meeting with AIPAC about opposing the ICC
arrest warrants: _" AIPAC's longstanding opposition to the ICC's hostility
toward Israel is a policy position that predates this tweet by years and does
not reflect what was discussed in this meeting._

Rafi Barak did not respond to our request for comment.
